title: Usernames and referrers
prompt: Show every username, and the id of the user who invited them, renamed invited_by. Users nobody invited must show NULL.
hints: This needs only one table, but keep all rows.
solutions: SELECT u.username, r.id AS invited_by FROM users u LEFT JOIN users r ON r.id = u.referrer_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT u.username, r.id AS invited_by FROM users u JOIN users r ON r.id = u.referrer_id;
SELECT u.username, u.id AS invited_by FROM users u;

title: Sale details
prompt: For every order item, show its product's name, the order's date, and the quantity.
hints: Join order_items to two other tables.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT p.name, o.order_date, i.quantity FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id JOIN orders o ON o.id = i.order_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT p.name, o.order_date, i.quantity FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id JOIN orders o;
SELECT i.product_id, o.order_date, i.quantity FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON o.id = i.order_id;

title: No grade yet
prompt: A student has an unfinished enrolment when it has no grade. Show each student_id with unfinished enrolments and how many, as unfinished.
hints: No join is needed. Filter, then count.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT student_id, COUNT(*) AS unfinished FROM enrolments WHERE grade IS NULL GROUP BY student_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT student_id, COUNT(grade) AS unfinished FROM enrolments WHERE grade IS NULL GROUP BY student_id;
SELECT student_id, COUNT(*) AS unfinished FROM enrolments GROUP BY student_id;

title: Rainier than yesterday
prompt: Show each reading's id where rainfall was higher than the same city's rainfall on the previous calendar day.
hints: Join on the previous date, not the previous id.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: UPDATE readings SET rainfall_mm = 3.0 WHERE id = 2; UPDATE readings SET reading_date = '2024-03-08' WHERE id = 4; INSERT INTO readings VALUES (9, 'Oslo', '2024-03-07', 1, 0.5);

solutions: SELECT t.id FROM readings t JOIN readings y ON y.city = t.city AND y.reading_date = date(t.reading_date, '-1 day') WHERE t.rainfall_mm > y.rainfall_mm;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT t.id FROM readings t JOIN readings y ON y.id = t.id - 1 WHERE t.rainfall_mm > y.rainfall_mm;
wrongSolutions.why: The previous row isn't the previous day

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT t.id FROM readings t JOIN readings y ON y.city = t.city AND y.reading_date = date(t.reading_date, '-1 day') WHERE t.rainfall_mm < y.rainfall_mm;

title: Average session gap
prompt: Each user's first and last session are the earliest and latest date. Show each user_id and the days between them as span, rounded to 1 decimal.
solutions: SELECT user_id, ROUND(julianday(MAX(session_date)) - julianday(MIN(session_date)), 1) AS span FROM sessions GROUP BY user_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT user_id, ROUND(julianday(MIN(session_date)) - julianday(MAX(session_date)), 1) AS span FROM sessions GROUP BY user_id;
SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) AS span FROM sessions GROUP BY user_id;

title: Low or missing discount
prompt: Show each product's name and discount for order items whose discount is under 1 or wasn't recorded.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL); UPDATE order_items SET discount = 0.5 WHERE order_id = 12;

solutions: SELECT p.name, i.discount FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id WHERE i.discount < 1 OR i.discount IS NULL;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT p.name, i.discount FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id WHERE i.discount < 1;
SELECT p.name, i.discount FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id WHERE i.discount IS NULL;

title: Every attempt count
prompt: For every student and course, show student_id, name, title, and attempts, sorted by student_id then title. Pairs with none show 0.
hints: Grid, then LEFT JOIN, then group.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT s.id AS student_id, s.name, c.title, COUNT(e.id) AS attempts FROM students s CROSS JOIN courses c LEFT JOIN enrolments e ON e.student_id = s.id AND e.course_id = c.id GROUP BY s.id, s.name, c.id, c.title ORDER BY s.id, c.title;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT s.id AS student_id, s.name, c.title, COUNT(*) AS attempts FROM students s CROSS JOIN courses c LEFT JOIN enrolments e ON e.student_id = s.id AND e.course_id = c.id GROUP BY s.id, s.name, c.id, c.title ORDER BY s.id, c.title;

SELECT s.id AS student_id, s.name, c.title, COUNT(e.id) AS attempts FROM students s JOIN enrolments e ON e.student_id = s.id JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id GROUP BY s.id, s.name, c.id, c.title ORDER BY s.id, c.title;

title: Managers of many
prompt: Show the name of employees who manage at least 2 people.
hints: Group by manager, then look up the name.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test'); UPDATE employees SET manager_id = 13 WHERE id = 12;

solutions: SELECT m.name FROM employees e JOIN employees m ON m.id = e.manager_id GROUP BY m.id, m.name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT m.name FROM employees e JOIN employees m ON m.id = e.manager_id GROUP BY m.id, m.name HAVING COUNT(*) > 2;
SELECT e.name FROM employees e JOIN employees m ON m.id = e.manager_id GROUP BY e.id, e.name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2;

title: Shipping rate
prompt: A customer's shipping rate is their shipped orders divided by all their orders, and 0 if they have none. Show each customer's id as customer_id and rate, rounded to 2 decimals.
hints: LEFT JOIN, a conditional sum, and a safe default.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT c.id AS customer_id, ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN o.status = 'shipped' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(o.id), 0), 2) AS rate FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT c.id AS customer_id, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN o.status = 'shipped' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(o.id), 2) AS rate FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id;
wrongSolutions.why: Integer division, with NULL for no orders

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT o.customer_id, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN o.status = 'shipped' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(o.id), 2) AS rate FROM orders o GROUP BY o.customer_id;

title: Average price paid
prompt: Prices vary by product. For each product, show its id as product_id and its average price paid per unit as average_price: total price times quantity, divided by total units. Products with no sales show 0. Round to 2 decimals.
hints: A weighted average needs SUM divided by SUM.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT p.id AS product_id, ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(p.price * i.quantity) / SUM(i.quantity), 0), 2) AS average_price FROM products p LEFT JOIN order_items i ON i.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT p.id AS product_id, ROUND(SUM(p.price * i.quantity) / SUM(i.quantity), 2) AS average_price FROM products p LEFT JOIN order_items i ON i.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.id;
SELECT p.id AS product_id, ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(p.price * i.quantity) / SUM(i.quantity), 0), 2) AS average_price FROM products p JOIN order_items i ON i.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.id;

title: Average by course
prompt: Show each course's id as course_id and its average grade, rounded to 2 decimals, as average. Ignore courses with no enrolments.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (15, 8, 5, 61, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT c.id AS course_id, ROUND(AVG(e.grade), 2) AS average FROM courses c JOIN enrolments e ON e.course_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT c.id AS course_id, AVG(e.grade) AS average FROM courses c JOIN enrolments e ON e.course_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id;
SELECT c.id AS course_id, ROUND(AVG(e.grade), 2) AS average FROM courses c LEFT JOIN enrolments e ON e.course_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id;

title: Report summary
prompt: Show each manager's id as manager_id, name, their number of direct reports as reports, and the average salary of those reports rounded to a whole number as avg_salary, sorted by id.
hints: Self join, then group by manager.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test'); UPDATE employees SET salary = 70001 WHERE id = 12;

solutions: SELECT m.id AS manager_id, m.name, COUNT(*) AS reports, ROUND(AVG(e.salary)) AS avg_salary FROM employees e JOIN employees m ON m.id = e.manager_id GROUP BY m.id, m.name ORDER BY m.id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT m.id AS manager_id, m.name, COUNT(*) AS reports, ROUND(AVG(m.salary)) AS avg_salary FROM employees e JOIN employees m ON m.id = e.manager_id GROUP BY m.id, m.name ORDER BY m.id;
SELECT m.id AS manager_id, m.name, COUNT(*) AS reports, AVG(e.salary) AS avg_salary FROM employees e JOIN employees m ON m.id = e.manager_id GROUP BY m.id, m.name ORDER BY m.id;

title: February best sellers
prompt: Show the name of products with at least 2 units sold in February 2024, and those units as units.
hints: Filter the date range, then total per product.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL); UPDATE orders SET order_date = '2024-02-29' WHERE id IN (11, 12);

solutions: SELECT p.name, SUM(i.quantity) AS units FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON o.id = i.order_id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id WHERE o.order_date BETWEEN '2024-02-01' AND '2024-02-29' GROUP BY p.id, p.name HAVING SUM(i.quantity) >= 2;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT p.name, SUM(i.quantity) AS units FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON o.id = i.order_id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY p.id, p.name HAVING SUM(i.quantity) >= 2;

SELECT p.name, SUM(i.quantity) AS units FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON o.id = i.order_id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id WHERE o.order_date BETWEEN '2024-02-01' AND '2024-02-29' GROUP BY p.id, p.name HAVING SUM(i.quantity) > 2;
